withAbort(start, signal): if no signal, just calls start(); otherwise throwIfAborted, races Promise.resolve().then(()=>{throwIfAborted(); return start()}) against a cancellation promise from the abort event, re-checks throwIfAborted after the race, and always removes the abort listener in finally.

withAbort does not pass any cancellation token into start() itself -- start's returned promise is not cancelled, only the CALLER'S wait for it is short-circuited. If start()'s underlying operation (e.g. a Postgres query or MCP HTTP fetch) has no internal cancellation, it keeps running to completion in the background after withAbort has already rejected/returned to the caller.

mechanismRecords.f3Correction: The v1 audit's practicalBenefit/deltaBeyondCvf text implicitly endorsed the source comment's claim that 'DATABASE_URL itself never crosses' as an unqualified security property. This is corrected: `childEnv(env, passEnv)` builds its allowlist as `[...BASE_ENV_ALLOWLIST, ...passEnv]` at line 45, iterating a SINGLE combined list with no distinction in how baseline names versus operator-supplied passEnv names are treated -- for ANY name in that combined list, `if (env[name] !== undefined) out[name] = env[name]` copies the value under its OWN name. The comment 'DATABASE_URL itself never crosses' is true only for the specific case where 'DATABASE_URL' is NOT itself listed in BASE_ENV_ALLOWLIST or in the operator's passEnv array (the baseline array indeed omits it, relying instead on the explicit remap at line 47: `if (!out.MEMORABLE_DB_URL && env.DATABASE_URL) out.MEMORABLE_DB_URL = env.DATABASE_URL`). But passEnv() at lines 76-81 validates candidate names ONLY against `ENV_NAME = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/` with no deny-list, no special-case rejection of 'DATABASE_URL', and no cross-check against the values BASE_ENV_ALLOWLIST already remaps specially. An operator who writes `passEnv: ["DATABASE_URL"]` in a provider config therefore causes `out.DATABASE_URL = env.DATABASE_URL` to be set directly at line 45, under its own literal name, before the separate conditional MEMORABLE_DB_URL fallback, which runs after the loop; a pre-existing truthy MEMORABLE_DB_URL is retained. This is a genuine, source-confirmed contradiction between the code comment's unqualified claim and the code's actual behavior under a realistic operator-configuration input, not merely a theoretical edge case: passEnv exists specifically so operators can extend the allowlist, and nothing in the validation layer stops them from choosing a name the baseline path was designed to specially remap instead of pass through raw.
